programs.haiku:
"""Layer-0 MLP down_proj component 1280: a "be"-word detector.

What it does, in plain terms: this component writes a strong "the word is 'be' (or 'been')"
signal into the residual stream. It reads the current token only (plus the token just before it,
to see whether 'be' follows a modal or 'will'), and predicts its activation:

  * "be" / "been" and its translations (быть, être, été, ser, essere):
      about 1.35 after a modal or negation (can be, must be, should not be, could be),
      about 0.9 after "to" (to be), about 0.45 after will/would ('ll be),
      about 0.55 otherwise; "been" is about 1.1 everywhere (has been, have been).
  * death words are negative: "died" and "死" about -3, "dead", "death", "dying", "dies",
      "deaths" about -1.2, "killed" and "alive" about -0.7, "die" about -0.4.
  * setup/configuration nouns and participles (arrangement, configuration, placement, setup,
      placed, arranged, setting, configured, 设置, 配置, 装置) about +0.6.
  * every other token predicts 0.

Only the current token and the previous one (in the same document) are read.
"""
READS = ()

BE_WORDS = {" be", "be", " been", "been", " быть", " être", " été", " ser", " essere"}
MODAL_LIKE = {" can", " could", " cannot", " must", " should", " may", " might", " shall", " also",
              " only", " not", " never", " always", " still", " even", " then", " Can", " Must"}
WILL_LIKE = {" will", " would", "'ll", "’ll", "will"}
SETUP_WORDS = {" arrangement", " arrangements", " configuration", " configurations", " placement",
               "配置", " setup", " placed", " arranged", " setting", " configured", " configure",
               " positioning", " placing", " arrange", "设置", "装置", "安置"}
DEATH = {" died": -2.9, "死": -3.0, "死亡": -1.4, " death": -1.2, " Death": -0.5, " dead": -1.2,
         " Dead": -1.0, " dying": -1.3, " dies": -1.0, " Died": -1.5, " killed": -0.7,
         " alive": -0.6, " deaths": -1.0, " die": -0.4, " Die": -0.6, "Die": -0.5}


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    tok = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    same_doc = len(prefix) > 1 and prefix.document_ids[-2] == prefix.document_ids[-1]
    prev = prefix.token_strings[-2] if same_doc else ""
    if tok in BE_WORDS:
        if tok in (" been", "been"):
            return None, 1.1
        if prev in MODAL_LIKE:
            return None, 1.35
        if prev in WILL_LIKE:
            return None, 0.45
        if prev == " to":
            return None, 0.9
        return None, 0.55
    if tok in SETUP_WORDS:
        return None, 0.6
    if tok in DEATH:
        return None, DEATH[tok]
    return None, 0.0

Known words and cognates give positive pulses, largest for 'principal'. Carry
extends them onto attached word endings and local 'principal of' or 'chief
executive officer' phrases. Independently, empty parentheses inside one token
respond, less strongly with extra punctuation or line breaks. Reset memory at
document boundaries. Ignore the many smaller, unrelated lexical fluctuations.

def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    document = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    previous, earlier = '', ''
    if carry is not None and carry[0] == document:
        previous, earlier = carry[1:]
    text = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = text.strip().lower()
    value = PULSES.get(word, 0.0)

    # Attached endings of split principle/principal words and Russian cognates.
    if text[:1].isalpha():
        if previous in ('princip', 'incip'):
            value = 0.9
            if word == 'led':
                value = 1.6
            elif word == 'ally':
                value = 2.0
        elif previous in ('глав', 'принцип', 'основ'):
            value = 0.4

    # Pulses continuing into short title and principle phrases.
    if word == 'of':
        if previous == 'principal':
            value = 1.85

            value = 0.7
    elif word == 'executive' and previous in ('principal', 'chief'):
        value = 0.75
    elif word == 'officer' and 'chief' in (previous, earlier):
        value = 0.85

    if '()' in text:

        value *= 0.25 ** (text.count('(') - 1)
        if '\n' in text:
            value *= 0.67 * 0.9 ** (text.count('\n') - 1)
        for mark, factor in ((';', 0.82), (',', 0.85), ('{', 0.65)):
            if mark in text:
                value *= factor
    return (document, word, previous), value

"""layers.0.mlp.down_proj:1286 as an "s + vowel" sound detector, sharpened for word pieces.

The component writes a negative value into the residual stream when the current token
carries a syllable that sounds like "sa" (or another s-vowel syllable, such as "se", "so"):
  * Latin-script tokens containing "sa" in any case (sa, SA, Sal, San, USA, ISA, esa, ...)
    give a negative value; it is strongest when the token continues a word that started in
    the previous token (no leading space, e.g. "Dioc|esan", "endorse|r"): -0.5, against
    about -0.15 for a token that starts a word;
  * Japanese, Korean and Chinese syllables with an s-sound (さ サ せ セ そ ソ す 萨 薩 素 사 소 서)
    give a negative value of about -0.25, largest on さ, サ, 萨 and 사;
  * other Latin tokens with s followed by e, o or u (ser, sor, so, se, su) give a weak
    negative value, mostly when they continue a word.
Everything else predicts 0. Values are class means measured on training text.
"""

import re

READS = ()

S_SYLLABLE_CHARS = frozenset("さサせセそソす萨薩素사소서")
WORD_END = re.compile(r"[A-Za-z]$")


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    word = token.strip().lower()
    # A token continues a word when it has no leading space and the token before ends in a letter.
    continues = not token.startswith(" ") and len(prefix.token_strings) > 1 and bool(
        WORD_END.search(prefix.token_strings[-2])
    )
    if token.strip() in S_SYLLABLE_CHARS:
        value = -0.25
    elif "sa" in word:
        value = -0.5 if continues else -0.15
    elif re.search(r"s[eou]", word):
        value = -0.09 if continues else -0.01
    else:
        value = 0.0
    return carry, float(value)

"""A small lexical proxy for a recurring sibilant-like trigger in this component.
It gives a modest negative score to tokens containing an s/z sound marker. This is
not a transcription system; it only recognizes visible, familiar script patterns."""
READS = ()

LATIN_SIBILANTS = frozenset("sz")
CYRILLIC_SIBILANTS = frozenset("сзшщжцч")
JAPANESE_SIBILANTS = frozenset("さしすせそざじずぜぞ")


def is_sibilant_marked(text):
    lower = text.casefold()
    if any(ch in lower for ch in LATIN_SIBILANTS):
        return True
    if any(ch in text for ch in CYRILLIC_SIBILANTS | JAPANESE_SIBILANTS):
        return True
    for ch in text:
        code = ord(ch) - 0xAC00
        if 0 <= code < 11172 and code // 588 in (9, 10):
            return True
    return False


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    return None, -0.01 if is_sibilant_marked(token) else 0.0

"""Layer-0 MLP down-projection, hidden unit 1287: "the end of a comment line".

This unit is silent on almost every token. Its clear job: on a line break (newline) that
closes a line of comment text, it writes a negative value into the residual stream. The
comment may be a whole line (`// ...`, `# ...`, `-- ...`, `/* ...`, or a ` * ...` line of
a doc block) or a comment after code on the same line. A newline that ends the text of a
chat turn or tool response (`<|im_end|>`, `</tool_response>`) is also mildly negative.
Other newlines, and all other tokens, are about zero.

How negative a comment's newline is depends on the comment:
  * deeper indentation (a comment inside a function or class body) is more negative,
    about -0.2 per column, from about -1.1 at the left margin, capped at 12 columns;
  * a comment in plain words is more negative than one holding code, so commented-out

TOOL_RESPONSE_CLOSE = -0.09

    strings = prefix.token_strings
    t = prefix.position
    cur = strings[t]
    prev = strings[t - 1] if t > 0 else ""

        value += EMPTY_THINK_NEWLINES
    if cur == "\t":

    if cur == "3":

Cyrillic letter, with the rest arriving in the next token. Decoded as text, the text so
far then ends in the replacement character U+FFFD. This component switches on at the
token that opens such an unfinished character (the text becomes unfinished there). It is
silent on the tokens that finish a character, and on everything else.

from the last finished character before it:

    katakana, and this is where it fires hardest (about 6);
  - after another non-ASCII character (kana, kanji, Hangul, Cyrillic, ...): about 1.7;
  - after ASCII text (a space, a letter, a digit) or at the start of a document: about 0.8.

REPLACEMENT = "�"

    else:
        before = prefix.text_prefixes[t - 1]
    finished_now = now.rstrip(REPLACEMENT)
    finished_before = before.rstrip(REPLACEMENT)
    # this token opens an unfinished character: the text now ends mid-character, and either

    opens = now.endswith(REPLACEMENT) and (

    last = finished_now[-1:]  # last finished character before the unfinished one

Recent repeated spaces and separator punctuation raise the estimate;
letter/digit endings and tight runs of token pieces lower it. Common
English word classes, casing, document-wide spacing and mean token length
refine the estimate. A document-initial space is strongly positive.

Apply this rule only to a bare ASCII-space token or a space followed only
by replacement characters (usually incomplete UTF-8 fragments). Predict
zero on other tokens, omitting their smaller token-specific responses.
Reset all history and formatting counts at document boundaries.

JOINERS = frozenset('& and but nor or'.split())
PREPOSITIONS = frozenset(
    'about above around as at below between by for from in into of on '
    'over per since than through to under until with within'.split()
)
AUX_OR_LINKING_VERBS = frozenset(
    'am are be been being equal equals had has have is was were'.split()
)
MONTHS = frozenset(
    'apr april aug august dec december feb february jan january jul july '
    'jun june mar march may nov november oct october sep sept september'.split()
)
LABELS = frozenset(
    'chapter claim eq equation ex example fig figure item line no number '
    'page part pp section step table theorem'.split()
)


def boundary_value(history, n, spaces, leading_spaces, length):
    previous = history[-1]
    word = previous.strip()
    lower = word.lower()
    tail = word[-1:]
    gap = 0
    for token in reversed(history):
        if token.startswith(' ') or '\n' in token:
            break
        gap += 1

    # Local separators versus a tightly packed letter/number run.
    value = 0.3618
    value -= 0.4347 * previous.isspace()
    value -= 0.1180 * ('\n' in previous)
    value -= 0.2857 * (bool(word) and word.isascii())
    value -= 0.1486 * word.isupper()
    value += 0.0592 * word.islower()
    value -= 0.5017 * tail.isdigit()
    value -= 0.3179 * tail.isalpha()
    value += 0.3387 * (lower in JOINERS)
    value += 0.2659 * (lower in PREPOSITIONS)
    value += 0.1431 * (lower in AUX_OR_LINKING_VERBS)
    value += 0.2096 * (lower in MONTHS)
    value += 0.1938 * (lower in LABELS)
    value += 0.2875 * (tail == ',')
    value += 0.0815 * (tail == '.')
    value += 0.1497 * (tail in (':', ';'))
    value -= 0.0659 * (tail in ('(', '[', '{'))
    value -= 0.1029 * (tail in (')', ']', '}'))
    value -= 0.0324 * gap
    for window, weight in ((8, 0.0940), (16, 0.0586), (32, 0.0270)):
        value += weight * sum(s == ' ' for s in history[-window:])

    # Broader formatting and a small adjustment for the start of a document.
    value += (0.6730 * spaces + 0.4200 * leading_spaces - 0.0918 * length) / n
    value += 1.1832 / (n + 1) - 0.0196 * math.log1p(n)
    return max(-1.6, min(2.08, value))


def step(carry, prefix, upstream):
    doc = prefix.document_ids[-1]
    if carry is None or carry[0] != doc:
        history, n, spaces, leading, length = (), 0, 0, 0, 0
    else:
        _, history, n, spaces, leading, length = carry
    token = prefix.token_strings[-1]
    fragment = token.startswith(' ') and set(token.strip()) == {'�'}
    value = 0.0
    if token == ' ' or fragment:

            value = 0.91 if fragment else 2.076
        else:
            value = boundary_value(history, n, spaces, leading, length)
    carry = (doc, (history + (token,))[-32:], n + 1,
             spaces + (token == ' '), leading + token.startswith(' '),
             length + min(len(token.strip()), 12))
    return carry, float(value)

i.e. a BPE token that continues a word (no leading space) and is made only of Cyrillic
letters. Whole words, and Latin, digit or punctuation tokens, get 0. Within such a fragment

    consonant -> lower;

    п, м, б, ж, ч, щ, к, т, с) -> strongly positive; a sonorant (н, л, в, й) -> mid;

program is a short lookup on spelling classes, not a list of token ids. It is stateless:
it reads only the current token.

SONORANT_END = set("нлвй")          # mid-strength final consonants

    ("oe", "obs"): 0.93, ("oe", "son"): 0.38, ("oe", "V"): 0.18, ("oe", "S"): 0.28,
    ("V", "obs"): 0.54, ("V", "son"): 0.31, ("V", "V"): 0.09, ("V", "S"): 0.12,

the token itself, not on its context. Each token, decoded alone, is lowercased and stripped,
then matched against the families below; the first family that matches sets the activation.
The strongest responses are to the word "structure" (about 3.8) and "institution" (about 3.4);
the Chinese 结构/构/机构 and Korean 구 for "structure" are about as strong. Construction

organisation, mechanism, framework, build, init, the code token "str", and design-type nouns

one of the strong words (the "of" in "construction of") is about 0.7. Everything else is 0.

    ("instruct", 1.2),  # instruction, instructor: weaker than the structure family
    ("construct", 2.0),  # construct, construction, constructed
    ("struct", 3.0),  # structure, structural, structured, struct, infrastructure
    ("institution", 3.0),  # institution(s), institutional
    ("constitut", 1.7),  # constitution, constitute
    ("archit", 1.5),  # architecture, architect
    ("config", 1.1),  # config, configuration, _config
    ("organiz", 1.0),  # organization, organized
    ("organis", 1.0),  # organisation (British spelling)
    ("mechanism", 1.0),
    ("framework", 0.9),
    ("build", 0.7),  # build, built, building, _build
    ("system", 0.5),  # system, systems
    ("schem", 0.7),  # schema, scheme
    ("layout", 0.7),
    ("arrang", 0.5),  # arrangement, arranged
    ("composition", 0.6),
    ("compris", 0.5),  # comprising, comprises
    ("consist", 0.5),  # consists, consisting
    ("setup", 0.9),
    ("assembl", 0.5),
    ("tissue", 0.6),
    ("apparatus", 0.7),
    ("district", 0.7),
    ("distribution", 0.6),
    ("design", 0.4),
    ("apparatus", 0.7),
    ("circuit", 0.7),
    # Chinese, Korean, Russian, Vietnamese words for structure, organisation, construction
    ("结构", 4.5), ("結構", 4.5), ("構", 4.0), ("构", 3.0), ("機構", 4.0), ("机构", 4.5),

    if word in WORDS:
